primary_paper.locations: Section 1 defines the positive-integer sum-product problem; Table 2 gives n=32, |A+A|=154, |AA|=154 and Psi_35^5 minus {75,81,100}; the text says these dataset minima are not known to be optimal.
primary_paper.computational_method: Section 2 reports examining every subset of [36], translated and dilated sets of bounded diameter, divisor-derived sets, and randomized sets. It says most exploration used Mathematica 14 and some speed-critical steps used Julia 1.10.
primary_paper.ai_provenance: The checked paper does not discuss generative-AI use. No stronger claim about the author's workflow is made here.

author_dataset_snapshot.note: The paper's v2 abstract reports 1,162,868 sets. The retrieved file snapshot has 1,163,592 lines; these are separate version-specific counts. The entire file is not duplicated in this task.

saved_source_row.format: One brace-delimited set of comma-separated positive integers
saved_source_row.interpretation: The row equals Psi_35^5 minus {75,81,100}, with 32 elements. Its exact sumset and product-set sizes are both 154.

reproduced_witness.verification: Recomputed all ordered pairs of the 32 integers using Python arbitrary-precision integer addition and multiplication; obtained 154 distinct sums and 154 distinct products.

open_status.evidence: The v2 paper explicitly says its tabled minima are not known to be optimal and its dataset is incomplete. The checked 2026 small-set paper arXiv:2601.21828 proves exact values only for cardinalities 10 and 11; it does not settle cardinality 32.
open_status.limitation: The 154 construction is a feasible upper bound for this minimization task, not a proof of the minimum.
